title: PBMC Isolation from Apheresis Collars
author: Girija Goyal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.56bg9an
materials: Dilute 100x by adding 10ul cell solutions to 890 ul media in a 1ml eppendorf tube and 100ul Trypan blue

steps.title: Collect Blood from Collar
steps.instruction: Acquire the collar and make an incision to drain the blood into a 50mL conical tube.

steps.title: Dilute Blood Product
steps.instruction: Dilute the blood product with 2X volume of RPMI or PBS and mix well.

steps.title: Layer and Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Slowly layer the diluted solution on top of 10 mL density gradient solution and centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 300 g for 25 minutes at room temperature
Set acceleration and deceleration levels to minimal

steps.title: Collect PBMCs
steps.instruction: Remove the white layer of PBMCs using a 5 mL pipette tip and add the cells to 10 mL warm media in a 50 mL tube.

steps.title: Wash Cells
steps.instruction: Wash the cells by centrifuging, adjusting volume if the initial Leukopak volume was high.

substeps.instruction: If using 5 ml or more of the Leukopak, fill the tube to 50 mL to effectively wash the high number of cells
Centrifuge at 120 g for 10 minutes to remove platelets
Return acceleration/deceleration levels to high or 9

steps.title: Resuspend Cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate the media and resuspend the cells in warm media.

substeps.instruction: Use 20 mL warm media per 10 ml of starting blood product

steps.title: Count Cells
steps.instruction: Count the cells using a hemocytometer by counting the number of cells in each of the four quadrants.

substeps.instruction: Calculate total cells using the formula: total # of cells = (cells counted /4) X dilution factor X 10^4 cells/ml

steps.title: Store Cells
steps.instruction: Keep cells in solution in the refrigerator for up to two hours.
